interpretation: This unit is best read as the author's proposed change of proof representation: replace local pictures near individual zeros with fundamental domains mapped conformally to slit planes, then organize zeta's inverse behavior by the asserted accumulation of those domains at the sole essential singularity at infinity. The representation would give a global continuation framework, but it suppresses exact zero locations and the unit supplies no implication from the domain decomposition to the critical line.
source_support: The span reviews meromorphic continuation, the pole at 1, zero classes, and the functional equation; defines fundamental domains as regions conformally mapped onto a slit plane; attributes a general fundamental-domain program and an enriched Picard result to earlier work; and then says zeta's domains should accumulate only at infinity.
nonparaphrase_operation: Reframes the pointwise zero problem as an inverse-domain decomposition while separating the organizational gain from the missing theorem that would constrain nontrivial zeros.
speculation_status: The general domain theorem is reported from prior work, the accumulation statement is asserted, and any resulting restriction on zero placement or proof of RH remains only the author's announced research program in this unit.
quality_reason: Accepted after revision because the prose supports the global-representation reading, with cited and announced claims kept distinct; degraded contour, Laurent, and functional-equation typography is not used to infer any additional result.

interpretation: The source uses continuation of real-axis inverse images to build a curve-and-strip skeleton rather than to re-prove zero simplicity. The quasi-lacunary value 1 separates boundary curves whose images approach 1 at infinity from interior components whose continuation covers the whole real axis; conditional on the cited continuation and uniqueness results, this organizes zeros and preimages of 1 strip by strip. The skeleton localizes selected fibers of zeta but does not retain the full two-dimensional map or independently validate the stated strip inventory.
source_support: The span explicitly says it repeats results from [3], cites [9] for simple zeros, colors inverse images of the two real half-axes, defines 1 as quasi-lacunary, and states that consecutive boundary curves form strips. It later cites [3], Theorem 7, for the unique component Gamma_{k,0}, bijectivity properties, and the j_k counts of curves, nontrivial zeros, and preimages of 1.
nonparaphrase_operation: Extracts the dependency structure by identifying value 1 as the selector for boundary versus interior continuations and by showing that the finite strip inventory is conditional on cited global curve properties, not a consequence of the displayed construction alone.
speculation_status: Simplicity, unboundedness and nonintersection of the curves, uniqueness and bijectivity, and the j_k inventory are cited or asserted rather than proved here. Theorem 1's proof also leaves unproved the step that a domain formed if two boundary curves met would have to contain a pole.
quality_reason: Accepted after revision because the quasi-lacunary-value mechanism and conditional strip organization are recoverable from the prose; damaged conjugation marks and curve notation preclude stronger literal claims but do not prevent this bounded interpretation.

interpretation: The source's red/black rule records whether a real-axis preimage branch maps to the negative or positive half-axis. It uses the required alternation first to claim a tail restriction and real critical-point interlacing, then combines a limiting-ray argument with the distinguished component Gamma_{k,0} to characterize an unbounded component of the closed-unit-disc preimage. This encoding gains adjacency and sign information while discarding most value-plane phase data; crucially, uniqueness comes from the previously asserted uniqueness of Gamma_{k,0}, not from color alternation by itself.
source_support: Theorem 2 states that both half-axis branches lie at negative real part far along their tails and gives only a one-paragraph circle-preimage argument. The span then claims simplicity and alternation of real zeros of zeta prime, and Theorem 3 explicitly concludes its uniqueness statement from the limiting-ray correspondence and the uniqueness of Gamma_{k,0}.
nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes the argument into sign-color adjacency, a ray-limit criterion for unboundedness, and an inherited uniqueness premise, exposing which conclusion each mechanism can and cannot support.
speculation_status: The tail necessity and the simplicity/interlacing inference are not adequately established by the short arguments in this unit. The unbounded-component conclusion remains conditional on the earlier asserted global continuation properties and uniqueness of Gamma_{k,0}.
quality_reason: Accepted after revision because the sign-color and limiting-ray mechanisms are legible without the figures, while the lightly degraded inverse-image notation and imported premises are explicitly bounded.

interpretation: The intended branch-cut construction grows inverse images of target circles around zero until contacts occur at critical points, then uses preimages of segments to the associated critical values as cuts that are supposed to divide a strip into one-to-one slit-plane pieces. This converts failures of local invertibility into proposed boundaries for inverse branches, but the span does not itself establish the incidence pattern, conformality, or one-simple-zero content of the resulting pieces.
source_support: The span states that small-circle preimages are disjoint closed Jordan curves around individual zeros, describes their fusion at points v_{k,j}, cites [3] and [9] for exactly j_k-1 such points, and says the resulting arcs and strip boundaries form fundamental domains Omega_{k,j}. It separately reports intertwined-curve, color-matching, and zero-simplicity results from [9].
nonparaphrase_operation: Interprets growing-circle collisions as candidate locations for branch cuts and audits the construction's dependency chain: even the initial one-zero Jordan curves rely on asserted simplicity and local one-zero behavior, while the later partition relies on cited counts and incidence rules.
speculation_status: Exact branch-point counts, conformality of the cut pieces, one-to-one intertwining, color matching, and simplicity are cited assertions rather than local conclusions. The intended construction is prose-recoverable, but unseen figures and degraded derivative notation prevent independent verification of those rules.
quality_reason: Accepted after revision because the concrete circle-growth and critical-value-slit mechanism is preserved without claiming that it identifies the partition exactly; all imported uniqueness, conformality, and simplicity claims remain visibly conditional.
